target_paper.title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias
target_paper.original_source: Table 1 (Sec. 5.2) GPT-4o row: ASR factual error 0.06, gender 0.16, fake reference 0.32, rich content 0.07; Human and Random rows for the directional statements; Table 5 (Appendix F.1) positional screen

generation.substitute_snapshot: the paper's judge is the API alias 'gpt-4o' accessed 2024.06 (Table 4); pinned here as gpt-4o-2024-05-13, the snapshot the alias resolved to at that date; substitute for the retired gpt-4-1106-preview / gpt-4-0613 judge arms
generation.six_vote_assumption: the paper reports 6 votes per pair with positions shuffled but not their composition for LLM judges; implemented as the 3 Appendix-E prompts x 2 answer orders (balanced placements as Appendix F.1 states); recorded as an assumption
generation.parameters: temperature 0 (unreported by the paper), max_tokens {'cot_first': 600, 'direct': 64, 'vote_first': 600}, no seed parameter, one pass; system prompt = Appendix E (sha256 cot_first 1b01298f227c, direct 126d0915587f, vote_first bbef3462cb5a); user message = Appendix E template with the released 'question' field and the two released answers verbatim
generation.battery: 4260 archived calls of 142 questions x (control + 4 perturbations) x 3 prompts x 2 orders = 4,260; votes per pair {6: 710}; vote parse modes {"strict": 3896, "subject": 286, "unparsable": 20, "however": 47, "lenient": 9, "tie-words": 1, "line": 1}

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 as the card instantiates it (originals inside item-bootstrap CIs + factual-error ASR <= 0.11 + fake-reference ASR < 0.37 = survived; fake-reference >= 0.37 or factual-error > 0.21 = dead; else partial); human double-coding pending
results.note: ASR per Sec. 4.6 (Eq. 2 reference/rich content, Eq. 3 factual error/gender) on 6-vote mean preferences with 0.5 -> Tie; item-level bootstrap over the 142 questions; comparison at the ASR level only because the original votes were not released

reproducibility_frictions_observed: judge model named only by alias ('gpt-4o', accessed 2024.06); dated snapshot inferred as gpt-4o-2024-05-13 - labelled substitute snapshot
the paper's 'GPT-4-Turbo' is gpt-4-1106-preview (retired) and 'GPT-4' is gpt-4-0613 (retired); neither judge arm can be re-run
6-vote composition for LLM judges not stated; assumed 3 prompts x 2 orders
judge decoding parameters (temperature, max tokens) unreported; temperature 0 assumed
no evaluation code and no original votes released; ASR re-implemented from Sec. 4.6 and validated against the Random row of Table 1
judge prompts exist only in the paper appendix (PDF listing with spacing artifacts); one escape ('by \n.') is ambiguous
106 of 142 factual-error perturbed answers carry a leading newline in the released data (extraction artifact); passed verbatim
rich-content perturbations were rendered for human judges; LLM judges receive raw markdown / emoji text, as in the paper
